title: 1. Variables & Basic Types
text:
In R, you create a variable with the assignment arrow <- (an equals sign = also works). R has a few core types: numeric, character (text), and logical (TRUE/FALSE). Use class() to check a value’s type.
Edit the code below if you like, then press Run Code to check your answer.

title: 3. Functions
text:
R comes with hundreds of built-in functions (sum(), sd(), sort()…), and you can write your own with function(...). The last evaluated expression inside a function is what it returns.

title: 2. Vectors
text:
A vector is R’s basic building block — an ordered collection of values of the same type, made with c(). Arithmetic on vectors happens element-by-element. Indexing uses square brackets and starts at 1, not 0.
Edit the code below if you like, then press Run Code to check your answer.

     92
     88
  
  Check Answer
  



  Q2. Fill in the blank: the idiomatic way to build the vector 1, 2, 3 is:

title: 5. Data Frames
text:
A data frame is R’s table type — a set of equal-length columns, each possibly a different type. This is what most real statistics and data analysis in R is built on.

title: R Programming
text:
Learn R, Live in Your Browser
A hands-on intro to R. Every example in this course is real, editable code that runs on a real R engine — powered by WebR, no install or server required.
Use the sidebar to move between lessons. Variables you create in one lesson are still available in later ones on the same page, just like a real R console — though each lesson page starts its own fresh session.
